claims.text: For \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\), the associated rectangle is \(i^j\), with \(i=s-t+1\) and \(j=r-t+1\). [source-2@L1354-L1362|claim=formal-document]

The nonidentity bigrassmannians are parameterized by \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\), and \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) is explicitly the permutation in lines 987–991. [source-2@L973-L992|claim=formal-document]

Put \(q=n-r\). The inverse correspondence is \[ t=r-j+1,\qquad s=i+r-j,\qquad n=r+q. \] The source admissibility conditions are equivalent to \[ 1\le i\le q,\qquad1\le j\le r. \] Indeed, admissibility gives \(i,j\ge1\), \(j\le r\), and \(t>r+s-n\iff q-i+1>0\iff i\le q\). Conversely, these rectangle bounds give \(1\le t\le r\), \(t\le s<n\), and \(t-(r+s-n)=q-i+1>0\).
This correspondence is injective: from \((r,s,t,n)\), recover \((q,i,j)=(n-r,s-t+1,r-t+1)\); from \((r,q,i,j)\), recover \((r,s,t,n)\) by the preceding inverse formulas.
Each prescribed generating family has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements, where \(a=\min(q-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-2@L1382-L1421|claim=formal-document]

1382:   Given a bigrassmannian $v=v_{r,s,t,n}$ in type $A_{n-1}$ with $\schubp_v = s_{i^j}$, let
1383: $$
1384: \begin{aligned}
1385: a&:=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\\
1386: b&:=\min(i,j).
1387: \end{aligned}
1388: $$
1389: 
1390: Then $J_v$ is generated as an ideal of 
1391: $H^{\star}(G/P_J, {\mathbb Z})\cong \Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$ by 
1392: \begin{equation}
1393: \label{generating-set-one}
1394: \{ s_{\mu}: i^j \subseteq \mu \subseteq ((i+a)^b,i^{j-b}) \}.
1395: \end{equation}
1396: 
1397: Alternatively, $J_v$ is generated by 
1398: \begin{equation}
1399: \label{generating-set-two}
1400: \{ s_{\mu}: i^j \subseteq \mu \subseteq (i^j,b^a) \}.
1401: \end{equation}
1402: \end{theorem}
1403: 
1404: We delay our proof of Theorem~\ref{J-generators} until Section~\ref{minconjsection}.
1405: 
1406: \noindent
1407: Note that in both of the asserted generating sets \eqref{generating-set-one} and \eqref{generating-set-two} for $J_v$,
1408: the shapes $\mu$ indexing the generators $s_\mu$ run through an interval between
1409: the $j \times i$ rectangular shape $i^j$ and the disjoint union of $i^j$ with a 
1410: smaller rectangle of shape $a \times b$ or $b \times a$. 
1411: In \eqref{generating-set-one} the smaller rectangle is to the right
1412: of the rectangle $i^j$, with both top-justified, while in \eqref{generating-set-two} the 
1413: smaller rectangle is below the rectangle $i^j$, with both left-justified.  
1414: Thus in both cases, the generating sets have size $\binom{a+b}{a}$
1415: and consist of generators whose multiset of degrees
1416: have generating function 
1417: $$
1418: \sum_\mu q^{|\mu|} = q^{ij} \qbin{a+b}{a},
1419: $$
1420: where $\qbin{a+b}{a}$ is a $q$-{\it binomial coefficient} or {\it Gaussian polynomial} 
1421: \cite[I.2 Exer. 3]{Macdonald}.

claims.text: For nonempty rectangles, \(\binom{a+b}{a}>1\) exactly when \[ 1\le i\le q-1,\qquad1\le j\le r-1. \]

Under the convention \[ \{r\le5,\ q\le6\}\setminus\{r\le4,\ q\le5\}, \] the 90 deduplicated bigrassmannian instances with \(\binom{a+b}{a}>1\) are \[ v_{5,\,i+5-j,\,6-j,\,q+5}, \quad 2\le q\le6,\ 1\le i\le q-1,\ 1\le j\le4, \] giving \(4(1+2+3+4+5)=60\) cases, together with \[ v_{r,\,i+r-j,\,r-j+1,\,r+6}, \quad 2\le r\le4,\ 1\le i\le5,\ 1\le j\le r-1, \] giving \(5(1+2+3)=30\) cases. The two families are disjoint since their \(r\)-values are respectively \(5\) and \(2,3,4\); injectivity proves there are no further duplicates.
The paper reports computer verification of minimality only for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2@L1495-L1502|claim=formal-document]
